findings: ETT.tex:1825-1830, under DEC-19, in the readings: the formula holds at every globally hyperbolic, Hausdorff, second countable E_{>=0}-manifold, with no Lean hypothesis left (Causal.SingularRowsK.cup_cap_BTZ). It also holds at every E_{>=0}-manifold whose causal futures J^+(z) are closed, with neither Hausdorff nor second countability (cup_cap_BTZ_of_isClosed). The row's existing finding said « no declaration instantiates it there yet »; that is now done. At E_0, take p = (0,0) on the BTZ line and p_n = (-1/(n+1), 0) → p along the axis from below. Then p ∉ J^-(p_n), and ⋃_N ⋂_{n>=N} J^-(p_n) = J^-(p) ∖ {p}, a non-empty set (nonvacuous_e0_cup_cap). The certificate of record, cupCapBTZAsPrinted_of_globallyHyperbolic, holds at E_0, and its antecedents hold there too: E_0 is a strongly causal SingularFlatSpacetime for SFALocal.sing E0 (nonvacuous_e0_certificate). So the printed, strongly causal form holds at E_0 (globally hyperbolic) and fails at E_0 ∖ {w} (CupCapBTZCounterexample). The finding behind DEC-19 is unchanged.

This is the sentence « including at BTZ points, where I^-(x) is empty and only K^-(x) can be dense ». So at every point strongly tarentin in the past, K^-(x) = I^-(x) (prop:tarentin_fort_K), (b) reads J^-(x) ⊆ cl I^-(x), and that classical density holds (hypothesis_b_tarentin). The existing finding on l.954 is unaffected: a local version of prop:tarentin_fort_K is not proved for a general M.

questions: ETT.tex:958-959, « where I^-(x) is empty and only K^-(x) can be dense »: the remark does not say dense in what. Reading taken: dense in J^-(x), as in hypothesis (b). At a BTZ point x, I^-(x) = ∅ is not dense in J^-(x) (which contains x), and J^-(x) ⊆ cl K^-(x) (hypothesis_b_btz). Under the other natural reading, « K^-(x) is non-empty near x and I^-(x) is not », the same theorem gives it. Low stakes: no other row depends on it.

ETT.tex:2082-2087, the argument (l.2090-2097): it does not need Σ to be a Cauchy surface. Any S such that J^+(S) is a neighbourhood of each point of J^+(S) ∖ S will do. Example: S = J^+(q) ∖ I^+(q) for a BTZ point q, where J^+(S) ∖ S = I^+(q) is open and non-empty (btz_cone_shell, from the model-free cone_shell). At E_0, with q = (0,0), it gives a non-vacuous instance (nonvacuous_e0_Sigma). The library has no splitting of E_0, so K_ordre_Sigma_of_splitting is not instantiated.
